input.question: If the coriolis effect makes hurricanes/typhoons swirl in different directions, what exactly happens when storms cross the equator? Do they begin to slow and weaken?
input.ground_truth: Look at [this chart](_URL_0_). Hurricanes don't cross the equator! They don't even form very close to the equator, because the Coriolis effect doesn't exist at the equator and is very small at small latitudes. As a storm approaches the equator, it either loses intensity or turns away because there is no driving force there to keep it going.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: If the coriolis effect makes hurricanes/typhoons swirl in different directions, what exactly happens when storms cross the equator? Do they begin to slow and weaken?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine the Earth is like a big spinning top. When it spins, it makes the air move in different ways. This is called the Coriolis effect.

Now, think of a toy top that spins. If you roll a marble around the top, it will go in a circle, but the direction it goes depends on which side of the top you roll it from.

Hurricanes and typhoons are like those marbles, but they are big, swirling storms. In the Northern Hemisphere (like the USA, Europe), these storms spin one way—let’s say, clockwise if you look down from space. In the Southern Hemisphere (like Australia), they spin the other way—counterclockwise.

Now, if one of these big storms crosses the equator (the imaginary line that goes around the middle of the Earth), it kind of “switches sides” of the spinning Earth. So, the way it spins changes! It starts going the other way around.

But, crossing the equator doesn’t make the storm slow down or get weaker right away. It just changes the direction it spins. It’s like if you rolled your marble from one side of the spinning top to the other—it still keeps rolling, but now it goes the opposite way.

So, when a storm crosses the equator, it just starts swirling the other way, but it doesn’t necessarily get weaker unless other things happen, like if it goes over land or doesn’t have warm water anymore.
